_comment: Self-paced improvement roadmap for the cheat-sheet app. Autonomous multi-session build: each batch is implemented fully, tested, committed, then a wakeup is scheduled ~1min later to continue with the next pending batch. HARD RULE (from owner): 100% local, ZERO external runtime dependencies, NO AI/cloud features. gzip etc. must use Node built-ins (zlib). HTB/THM checklists are authored at build-time and baked as STATIC data — the app never phones home. On each wakeup: read this file, pick the first 'pending' batch, implement it, run `npm test`, commit with a 'feat:'/'fix:' message, mark 'done', schedule next wakeup.
owner_priorities: Tag filter under the search box is buggy — must work correctly

Overhaul Write-ups AND Machines (design + functionality). Machines: situation-aware checklists (Linux/Windows privesc, Web, AD multi-machine with captured creds/loot, etc.) baked from HTB/THM/OSCP methodology; strong visual presentation that references the next steps while solving a box

constraints.built_ins_only_for_perf: use node:zlib for compression, no 'compression' package
constraints.typescript_devdep: avoid — keep dependency-free (JSDoc only if ever needed)

batches.title: AD environment — full professional engagement model (owner follow-up on #2a)
batches._note: Owner feedback after batch 6: the AD support was only a flat host list + attack-path text. Owner wants a REAL, professional engagement model. Build it properly, not tokenistically.
items: Each AD host is a FULL sub-target: its own OS/role, its own playbook + phase checklist (reuse templateToChecklist), its own loot/creds, notes, and owned status — not just name/ip. Click a host to expand/work its checklist inline; per-host progress shown.
Link EXISTING machines as hosts: pick from the machine list to attach one as a host in the engagement (store a reference/copy), plus create-new-host inline. Avoid duplication footguns.

Interconnected SCHEMATIC view: a vanilla-JS/SVG node-link diagram of the engagement — DC highlighted, owned hosts colored, edges = pivots/attack path (editable relationships model, e.g. host.links = [hostId]). Deterministic layout (radial/grid), no external libs. Clicking a node focuses that host.
Engagement-level overview: total hosts, owned count, aggregate checklist progress across hosts, and the current objective (e.g. path to DA).

Persist new structure via server (extend machine schema: hosts[] with checklist/loot/os/role/links). Keep backward compatibility with batch-6 flat hosts (migrate {name,ip,os,owned} rows gracefully). Add tests.
Strong, realistic visuals reusing batch-4 tokens; keyboard/aria per batch-5. Must feel like a genuine AD engagement workspace.

batches.title: Write-up report formats — genuinely professional templates (owner follow-up on #2b)
batches._note: Owner feedback: batch-7 write-up templates were basic section skeletons. Owner wants FULLY professional report formats. Author real, complete, industry-standard STATIC templates — not tokenistic.
items: Rewrite WRITEUP_TEMPLATES with genuinely professional, complete report structures (static, offline). At minimum: (1) OSCP exam report — administrative info, high-level summary, methodology, per-target vulnerability details with proof.txt/local.txt placeholders, steps to reproduce, maintaining access, house cleaning, appendices; (2) HTB/CTF write-up — machine info box, recon (nmap), enumeration, foothold with numbered steps, privesc, flags, beyond-root/lessons; (3) Pentest engagement report — executive summary, scope & rules of engagement, findings summary TABLE with severity, per-finding detail (description/impact/evidence/CVSS/remediation/references); (4) Bug bounty report — title, summary, steps to reproduce, impact, PoC, remediation.
Add a severity/CVSS helper: quick-insert a findings table row and severity badges; a small static CVSS v3.1 qualitative scale reference.
Insert-section menu (append individual sections like 'Add Finding', 'Add Target') beyond whole-template insertion.
Ensure the markdown renderer handles tables (| a | b |) so the findings tables render in preview/export; keep XSS-safe.
Professional print/PDF stylesheet for reports (headings, tables, page structure) reusing existing export path.
Reuse batch-4 tokens + batch-5 a11y; keep everything local and static.
